pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher Welcome Message - Kemble Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome Message
Welcome to our school. I am immensely proud to be Headteacher of such a special and caring community, where every child is known, valued and encouraged to be the very best they can be.
I have been a teacher for nearly 30 years, and throughout my career I have remained deeply passionate about education and the difference it can make to children’s lives. I understand the trust that families place in us and the vital role that strong relationships between home and school play in helping children thrive.
We see our school as a family, where children, families and staff work together in partnership. Our families are just as important to us as our pupils, and we believe that by supporting one another, listening openly and working collaboratively, we create the best possible environment for every child to succeed.
At the heart of our work is a strong commitment to promoting the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. These values run through our curriculum and school life, helping to develop independent, inquisitive thinkers who care about the world around them and about other people. We want our pupils to grow into confident, compassionate individuals who understand their responsibility to themselves, their communities and the wider world.
We are an academy and part of The Corinium Education Trust, a family of schools with the shared vision to Inspire, Challenge and Transform lives. Further information regarding the Trust including Trustee information, Accounts and Reporting can be found here.
We are an inclusive school where everyone is valued equally. We celebrate diversity, respect individuality and ensure that every member of our school community feels safe, welcomed and supported.
Our school is truly unique. Set within beautiful countryside, we recognise how special our environment is and make the most of it. Our curriculum embraces outdoor learning, using our wonderful outdoor spaces to enrich learning, inspire curiosity and promote wellbeing.
We are incredibly proud of our school and of the warm, ambitious and nurturing place it continues to be. We look forward to welcoming you and your family into our school community.
Mrs Jo RogersHeadteacher

Alongside the academic and global learning, we want our children to be happy while with us and to develop a ‘wellbeing’ toolkit to take them on into adolescence and adulthood. Our approach is built around the importance of self-knowledge and an understanding of the needs of others.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club (BC) and After School Club (ASC)
Who’s Who
Breakfast Club – Mrs Savage runs our breakfast club from 7:30am to 8:30am each day. They will welcome the children, offer them a healthy breakfast (treats too!) and have fun and games with your children. They can play outside in our wonderful playground and garden when the weather is good.
After School Club – Mrs Perkins and Mrs Rendell run after school club from 3:00pm to 5:30pm each day (apart from the last day of T2, T4 and T6 when cleaning is carried out). They will welcome the children after school and offer a range of craft, games and activities and outside play too. They have a healthy snack together – a super social time.
Both our clubs are held in the Willow Room with secure entrance and exit for families – separate from the school entrance.
Voucher Payments
We accept voucher payments for Breakfast Club and After School Club. Please contact the school office if your childcare voucher provider needs any details to be provided by the school. We are already set up to receive Edenred, Computershare, Caboodle and The Salary Exchange voucher payments and are also set up with HMRC Tax Free Childcare payments.
Once you have made a payment via your childcare voucher provider please can you email the school office at admin@kemble.gloucs.sch.uk to advise the amount that you have transferred, the voucher code, the date it will land in the account and how you wish for that amount to be allocated between Breakfast Club and After School Club. The office will then manually credit your ParentPay account as requested. The only further action required from you is that you monitor your ParentPay account to check that there is enough credit in the account to cover costs at all times.

Governors’ Information and Duties
Welcome to our Governors’ section
The role of the Local Governing Body is to provide focused governance for the school at a local level. We monitor the school’s key performance indicators and act as a critical friend to the Head Teacher, providing challenge where appropriate. We also play a part in representing the views of all the school stakeholders: children, staff and parents; as well as offering assistance to the Academy Trustees in the fulfillment of their duties.
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor.

SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disability) Information
Our Core Offer
Kemble Primary School Parent Information: Local School Offer
This offer is common to schools within the South Cotswold Schools Partnership.
Kemble Primary School values the contribution that every child can make and is supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress. The school seeks to raise the achievement, remove barriers to learning and increase physical and curricular access to all. All children and young people with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) are valued, respected and considered equal members of the school.
As such, provision for pupils with SEND is a matter for the school as a whole. All teachers are teachers of pupils with SEND. The Governing Body, Headteacher, SENDCO and all other members of staff are responsible for teaching children with SEND. This local offer is in line with the school SEND policy which can be accessed via the website or by contacting the school office.
SEN info and offer
Date of creation
No options...
SEN info leaflet
Who are the best people to talk to in this school about my child’s difficulties with learning/Special Educational Needs or Disability?
Special Educational Needs and Disability Coordinator (SENDCo)
At Kemble Primary School the SENDCO has responsibility for the overall management of SEND in the school. They are responsible for:
Class Teacher
The Class Teacher is responsible for:
Informing you of progress at Parent’s Evenings
Headteacher
The Headteacher is responsible for:
SEND Governor
The SEND Governor is Gemma Bull. She will be kept informed of SEND in the school by the SENDCo, Headteacher and the SENDCo’s annual report. She will make sure that the necessary support is made for any child who attends school who has SEND.
How can I let the school know I am concerned about my child’s progress in school?
How will the school let me know if they have a concern about my child’s learning and progress in school?
Regular meetings with staff are held to discuss the progress of all children to identify if any children are regularly causing concern. Areas of concern are monitored by the class teacher and SENDCO. If your child is identified as not making progress, the school will set up a meeting to discuss this with you in more detail. During this meeting the school will listen to any concerns you may have, plan and explain any additional support your child may receive and discuss with you any planned referrals to outside agencies. The SENDCo may attend this meeting, or may meet with you at a later date to discuss progress and outcomes of any initial support.
How is Kemble Primary School accessible to children with SEND?
Classroom equipment is accessible to all children regardless of their needs, and where additional needs are identified (visually impairment) further advice is sought.Extra Curricular activities are available and accessible to children with SEND.Children with specific needs will have additional members of staff to help them access the school, curriculum and clubs.
What are the different types of support available for children with SEND at Kemble Primary School?
Provision for each child is met on an individual basis. Some children will have support in class; others will be withdrawn for short periods to cover individual work, while some will work on a differentiated curriculum in groups.
Class Teacher input: Teachers endeavour to provide excellent classroom practice.
Specific Group work with a smaller group of children
Specified Individual support
How is extra support allocated?
How are the teachers in school helped to work with children with an SEND and what training do they receive?
Services who visit the school to help with support/advice and training:
Parent Support Advisor
Occupational Health Service
Educational Psychology Service
School Nurse
Specialist Health Advisors (e.g. Diabetes team)
Speech and Language team
How will the school measure the progress of your child in school?
The school is committed to continually monitoring the progress of all the children in the school.
This takes place in a number of ways:
How will teaching be adapted for my child with SEND?
All pupils have the right to a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum. All pupils with SEND are taught with their peers in mainstream classes by the class teacher, and study the curriculum appropriate for their needs. All teaching and support staff are aware of the Early Years Foundation Stage Statements and the National Curriculum Statements and in their planning and teaching they strive to:
Teachers match the learning objectives to the needs and abilities of the pupils. They use a range of strategies to develop the pupil’s knowledge, understand and skills. Where appropriate materials are modified or support is provided to enable pupils with SEND to access the learning or the assessment process.
Specific resources and strategies may be used to support your child individually and in groups.
The school acknowledges that its practices make a difference and because of this the school and teachers regularly review issues related to pupils with SEND and classroom organisation, teaching styles and methods, materials and tasks to determine how these can be improved.

pageCache.pageTitle: The School Day - Kemble Primary School
pageCache.text:
The School Day
Our School Day
Our school day runs from 8:45am-3:15pm which amounts to 32.5 hours a week.
Gates open for children to go into class
Breakfast Club
We run a daily breakfast club from 7:30am to 8:30am.You child will receive a healthy breakfast with a daily selection of fresh fruit, muffins, toast or crumpets, cereal with orange juice or milk. They can play games with friends, read or use the laptops.
After-School Club
We run a fun, relaxed after-school club from 3:15-5.30pm where children can play games, board – games or sports, construction toys or art activities. They might go on a treasure hunt in the school grounds or a nature walk. There are opportunities for debating and cooking too! We offer a range of healthy snack foods and some treats!
Both of these have a fee – current prices and terms and conditions available from the school office (pre-booking only)
After school activities are also available – most provided as free ‘taster’ or hobby clubs- usually a range of sports and interests each term – the office has further details.
